label: GDPR Art. 30 — Records of processing activities
body: 1. Each controller … shall maintain a record of processing activities … containing:
(a) the name and contact details of the controller …;
(c) a description of the categories of data subjects and of the categories of personal data;
(d) the categories of recipients to whom the personal data have been or will be disclosed including recipients in third countries or international organisations;
(e) where applicable, transfers of personal data to a third country …;
(f) where possible, the envisaged time limits for erasure of the different categories of data;
(g) where possible, a general description of the technical and organisational security measures referred to in Article 32.

5. The obligations referred to in paragraphs 1 and 2 shall not apply to an enterprise or an organisation employing fewer than 250 persons unless the processing it carries out is likely to result in a risk to the rights and freedoms of data subjects, the processing is not occasional, or the processing includes special categories of data as referred to in Article 9 or personal data relating to criminal convictions and offences.

[Currency note: the European Commission's May 2025 GDPR simplification (omnibus) proposal would amend Art. 30(5) — a wider record-keeping exemption keyed to high-risk processing, with a proposed under-750-employee threshold. A pending proposal as of authoring; verify whether adopted before relying on the 250-person threshold.]
